what: J.B. Hunt is a North American transport and logistics company. Its largest business is intermodal, moving containers by rail for most of the journey and by truck at each end, which is cheaper and uses less fuel than trucking the whole way.
customers: Retailers, manufacturers and consumer goods companies moving freight across North America.
money: containers moved by rail and delivered by truck
fleets operated exclusively for one customer
freight brokerage and heavy goods home delivery
moat: A container fleet and long-standing rail partnerships that would take years to replicate, plus dedicated contracts that run for years regardless of spot freight rates.
risks: Freight volumes have been weak for three years
Revenue has fallen about 7% a year over three years
Intermodal pricing has been under pressure from cheap truckload rates
Brokerage has been lossmaking in the downturn
opportunities: Analysts see about 24% upside from current levels
Return on invested capital of 12% with low debt
Intermodal gains share from trucking when fuel prices and driver costs rise
watch: Intermodal volumes and revenue per load.
